title: fix(gates): resolve a bare `export { X }` against the file's own imports
body:
Fixes #7275

## The rule

A bare `export { X }` is a barrel line too: the re-export arm now resolves the exported **local** name against the file's own imports and applies the existing barrel skip to it, so `export { X }` over `import { X } from './x'` is skipped exactly as `export { X } from './x'` already was.

`scanFile`'s skip read the export's **module specifier** (`if (fromModule && (fromModule.startsWith(".") || fromModule.startsWith("@object-ui/"))) continue;`). A bare `export { X }` has none, `fromModule` was `null`, the skip never fired, and the name was recorded as a `re-export` finding located **at the barrel** — pointing a reader at the wrong file and putting the ALLOW / DEBT ratchets within reach of an edit to a barrel rather than to the shape, which is the failure mode the skip exists to prevent.

The import loop that builds `specBindings` now also records every binding's source module (`importedFrom`); nothing else about that loop changed. Alias form resolves by the local name (`propertyName ?? name`), so `export { X as Y }` is judged on `X`. Forms with a specifier are untouched.

### ⛔ What is deliberately NOT skipped

A blanket "skip every bare `export { X }`" would pass the first two cases below and silently delete the rest of rule 1. All four are pinned as fixtures:

| bare `export { X }` where `X` is bound by | result |
| --- | --- |
| a relative / `@object-ui/*` import | skipped — judged at its declaration site |
| an `@objectstack/spec` import | derivation, via the unchanged `specBindings` arm |
| nothing (declared in this file) | still a visible finding |
| a third-party import | still a finding — this scan does not cover that module, so nothing else judges the name |

## Measured: before / after

Same corpus both runs, on this branch's base `d39ede24e` against `@objectstack/spec` 17.2.0 — **1348 files scanned against 4959 spec export names** in both.

| | rule 1 findings | declared dialects (ALLOW) | untriaged collisions (DEBT) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before | 36 | 20 | 14 in 7 packages |
| after | 35 | 19 | 14 in 7 packages |

The whole delta is one line:

```
- re-export ListView  packages/plugin-list/src/index.tsx:15
```

Every other finding in the tree is byte-identical (full dump diffed before and after; the removed row is the only one). Rule 2 and rule 4 are unmoved: `2 declared deliberate copies, 19 unbacked claims in 5 packages`, and no member citation.

## Ledger disposition

`@object-ui/plugin-list:ListView` was kept alive **by that barrel line alone** — the component at `ListView.tsx` is skipped structurally by `rendersJsx`. With the barrel attributed correctly the name matches nothing, and ratchet 3 said so on the run in between:

```
@object-ui/plugin-list:ListView is in ALLOW but no longer collides with a spec export name
```

So the entry is deleted, with a tombstone in the same shape as the two beside it recording what it carried beyond the waiver (`spec-symbol-batch6.test.tsx` still fails if the spec's `ListView` stops being authored metadata or if the export stops being a component that consumes it).

⛔ `@object-ui/auth:AuthProvider` and `@object-ui/plugin-list:UserFilters` are **not** re-added. #6291 deleted them because they matched nothing, and the corrected scan does not report them either — re-adding either would be a stale entry on the run that added it. Three entries written on one judgement; all three are now made structurally, and none of them is reachable by editing a barrel.

## Verification

- `node scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs` — before: exit 0, `20 declared dialects`; with the scanner fix but the entry still in ALLOW: exit 1, ratchet 3 (quoted above); final: exit 0, `19 declared dialects`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 scripts/__tests__/check-spec-symbol-derivation.test.ts` — **60 passed** (55 before, 5 new). It is the only file in the repo that imports the edited module; every other reference to it is prose.
- `pnpm type-check:scripts`, `pnpm lint:root` (0 errors), `pnpm check:control-bytes`, `check:entry-guard`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:shell-escape-residue`, `lint:coverage`, `type-check:coverage` — all exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` — `No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed.`
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` on both changed paths — `NOT GOVERNED`.

**Planted probe** (predicted, then observed), on the live barrel itself: `const NavigationConfig = { mode: 'page' }; export { NavigationConfig };` appended to `packages/plugin-list/src/index.tsx`. The gate reported **both** halves — `const NavigationConfig … :16` and `re-export NavigationConfig … :17` — in the same file whose sibling re-exports are now silent. Restored; blob hash back to the HEAD blob and `git diff HEAD` empty.

**Ablation** on the committed tree — the two new lines removed, mutation proven on disk (anchor count 1 → 0, blob `ba20382b` → `f01c6018`):

- fixtures: `2 failed | 58 passed` — cases (a) and (e), the two that depend on the branch; (b), (c), (d) stayed green, which is what says the ablation removed the resolution and not the arm.
- the gate: exit 1 — but **in the reverse direction from the run before the ledger edit**, and that is the honest reading. With the ALLOW entry now deleted, the reappearing barrel finding is not re-excused, it is *fresh*: `@object-ui/plugin-list declares 1 spec-named symbol the spec already owns: re-export 'ListView' packages/plugin-list/src/index.tsx:15`. The fix and the ledger edit hold each other up in both directions.
- restored: blob equal to the HEAD blob, `git diff HEAD` empty, anchor count back to 1.

All runs measured at `ab22b86d6`. Heavy runs went through the shared verify lock (`VERDICT command-exit 0`); wall-clock figures under it are shared-box readings.

## ⚠️ Overlap with an in-flight PR

Draft PR #7685 (#7122, head `7be4b2456`) carries one hunk on this same file, `@@ -670,46 +670,18 @@` in the ALLOW map, retiring the two #7580 `BreakpointName` / `BreakpointColumnMap` entries. My hunks are non-adjacent by construction — the re-export arm (~:1614–:1690), the `ListView` entry / tombstone (~:585–:616) and the rule-2 header clause — so a three-way merge is clean. Whichever lands second should merge `main` first, because both PRs move the `declared dialects` count the gate prints.

## Judgement, on the four axes

The only real choice here was the disposition of the three renderer entries, and specifically whether to keep `ListView`'s.

- **实际业务需求** — measured, not assumed: the entry excuses nothing after the fix (ratchet 3 quoted above), and its behavioural content is held by `spec-symbol-batch6.test.tsx`, which does not depend on the entry existing. Keeping it would serve no reader.
- **项目长远合理性** — deleting it is the contract-first move. The alternative (leaving it, or rewriting the barrel so it keeps matching) fixes the ledger at the barrel, which is exactly what this card says the scanner must stop being able to do.
- **防 AI 写代码犯错** — a stale ALLOW entry *reserves the name*: the next hand-written `ListView` under it would land silently. That is the tightening this repo prefers over a tolerant carry-over, and it is why the fix reports a local declaration twice (at its declaration and at its bare export) rather than teaching the scanner that a bare export is always someone else's problem.
- **创业阶段不扩散需求** — no new surface, no new flag, no transitional double spelling: one predicate shared by the two spellings of the same barrel line, and one entry fewer in the map.
